newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Relentless dollar buying from local importers and offshore speculators saw the rand take another hammering on Wednesday, sinking to a fresh all-time low on the dollar with traders expecting the fall to continue.
The currency ended the day more than five cents weaker at 4.7400/7450 on the dollar after hitting a new all-time low of 4.7410 bid and from 4.6865/15 at the Tuesday close.
Foreign exchange dealers said an assualt on the 4.75 level on the dollar was likely on Thursday as the currency remained sensitive to any volume moving through the market.
"Once we break 4.75 we could go to 4.78 and then to 4.80, although 4.80 looks toppish," a trader at a foreign bank said.
Another agreed, predicting that the rand should hold around 4.78/4.80 in the longer-term.
"The sooner we get there the better...we should see the rand level out at those levels," the second dealer said.
Traders said it was another hectic day on the currency market and trade was marked by heightened nervousness.
"Once the rand broke the 4.70 level sentiment took a dive and even though the Reserve Bank supplied dollars to the market it did not protect any levels," one said.
"There seems to be no end to the barrage of dollar demand," the dealer added.
Several traders noted that quite a few new offshore players had entered the market during the last few days.
Against the British pound the rand also hit a new record low of 7.7185/7314 from 7.5406/5529 on Tuesday.
Bond market yields moved above the 16 percent level for the second day running on the ailing rand after a promising start spurred by healthy U.S. Treasuries.
"The market started the day somewhat better on better U.S. rates but the rand dissapointed, breaking through 4.70, and bond market players started selling stock," a bond trader said.

He said there had been some support at the 16.02 percent level and in after-hours trade the yield on the key R150 bond managed to dip below the figure to trade at 15.96 percent from an intraday low of 16.03 percent, after 15.97 on Tuesday.
Bond traders said direction on Thursday would again be determined by the rand and players would also be keeping an eye on the U.S. market.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners sold a net 476.21 million rand worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 83.88 rand on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 8.12 billion rand from 5.39 billion rand on Monday.

On the money market, three-month NCD rate rose to between 16.50 and 16.20 percent from 16.30 to 16.15 percent on Tuesday. The 90-day BA rate was also higher at 15.80 to 15.60 percent from 15.70 to 15.55 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 8.722 billion rand on Tuesday from 8.359 billion rand on Monday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
